scenario: Reversible upgrade of a state created by the develop package, with kept workload markers, then explicit rollback and boot of the restored root

packages.build: release, Packaging/install-local.sh into one isolated prefix, ad hoc virtualization signing; opsmaru_incus 0.2.9 cassette downloaded and attestation-verified by the installer
packages.package_change: runtime stop, launchctl bootout of the server job then the runtime job, removal of the server plist only, install-local.sh of the target into the same prefix, then macus start (Packaging/homebrew/README.md sequence without Homebrew)

isolation.incus_conf: temporary directory created by Integration/scripts/start-acceptance.py (develop revision); every hand-run incus and macus start command exported it

workload_markers.default_project: container r53-marker with a random token in /root/marker, custom volume r53-vol attached at /mnt/vol with the same token, profile r53-profile with user.r53=marker
workload_markers.project_r53: container r53-proj-c with the token in /root/marker
workload_markers.after_upgrade: a second random token written to /mnt/vol/marker2 after the upgrade, before the rollback

steps.name: create_on_source
steps.note: The develop seed copies /var/log/tama-storage.log to the console 20 s after boot. On the provisioning boot tama-storage was still starting then, so the first boot wrote no TAMA_STORAGE_ZFS_READY line.

steps.name: start_on_target
steps.note: The develop guest serves the flow relay but reports no guest identity, so it was booted, probed and served; the Incus package came from the catalog entry.

checks.inventory: default: 1 instance, 2 volumes, 1 network, 2 profiles; r53: 1 instance, 1 volume, 1 network, 2 profiles

checks.rule: root only; data disk kept (backup Incus package equals the current data's)

findings: A state created by the develop package has no pool identity source until it has booted at least twice: the console copy of the storage log on the provisioning boot runs before storage is ready. Upgrading such a state while it is stopped after its only boot would be refused (no storage-identity.json, no serial line). Here the first start on the new package was the second boot and wrote the line, which is what made the upgrade possible; a develop guest's health never reports the identity itself.
For a reversible upgrade the plan prints 'keeping the backup can grow to 0 bytes'. The old root it keeps already occupies about 4 GiB, which the backup listing shows; the wording undersells that.
not_covered: Package rollback to the develop build after the state rollback (the state rollback and boot were run on the target package).
Migrating, failed and pre-relay upgrades (tasks 5.4 to 5.7).
